verdict.rationale: The proposal serves the North Star: Codex execute/fix was burning attention on no-op loops (same 78/79 RED) because the prompt forbade the only file channel that host has; ConPTY already covers the focus hazard. Gates, git, and tests stay orchestrator-owned in the authoring copy; review prompts are untouched; YOLO is opt-in and authoring-only. The patch matches those two behaviors and no more: authoringToolRule keeps the old ban unless FOREMAN_CODEX_CONPTY=1 and CODING_FAMILY=chatgpt; danger-full-access is allowlisted in the argv builder but resolveCodexSandbox still forces read-only for verification, synthesizer, unknown, and empty roles, and leaves default execute/fix at workspace-write. Windows unelevated is asserted absent on the YOLO argv path. No new transport, GO-rule edit, or product-plan change is in the diff.

findings.detail: Sharing one helper changes the default fix prompt on every host: it now appends '; strictly just edit the source files.' which the pre-patch fix string lacked. That is a tightening, not a widen, but it is not 'default text remains unchanged' as written.

The Codex exception still leads with 'Use dedicated file tools where available' and only then grants terminal when they are absent. That is the same search-first stall journaled for GPT-6-Astra; it matches the proposal's wording, so it is residual ineffectiveness risk, not a spec miss.
